summary: Autonomous driving is the visible front, but AI runs through freight matching, maritime navigation, transit operations, and aviation. Who tracks it: the safety regulators and standards bodies are the primary record, with the operators' own published data layered on top.

analysis.body:
Per the Census Bureau, 13.0% of transportation and warehousing firms (NAICS 48-49) reported using AI in the last two weeks in the latest Business Trends and Outlook Survey reading, up from 7.9% in the prior period. That is the broadest measured adoption figure available for the sector, and it captures everything from freight brokerage to warehousing to transit, not just the autonomous vehicle work that draws most public attention.

The most visible deployments are in autonomous driving. Aurora describes its Aurora Driver as built with verifiable AI and integrated into the Volvo VNL Autonomous, with a pilot program hauling freight autonomously between Fort Worth and El Paso in partnership with Werner. Waymo, which began as the Google Self-Driving Car Project in 2009 and served its first fully autonomous rides in 2015, publishes a safety program and supports the U.S. Department of Transportation National Roadway Safety Strategy. On the fleet operations side, Samsara reports its connected operations platform serves 20,000+ operations and that its AI-powered dash cams, real-time in-cab alerts, automated coaching, and drowsiness detection have contributed to 380,000+ accidents prevented. C.H. Robinson describes moving toward what it calls autonomous logistics orchestration, where the supply chain analyzes, decides, executes, and improves continuously across every shipment.

Vendor activity concentrates in a few layers. Aurora and Kodiak are identified in the source material as the pure-play autonomous trucking platforms running driverless corridors. Wärtsilä, a marine and energy equipment maker, points to AI-driven predictive analytics as one tool in its decarbonisation work for vessel operators. Airbus frames its innovation programs around a decarbonised, connected, and autonomous future for aerospace, working through digitised operations and an external innovation ecosystem. The World of AI's robotics models page tracks the 1,000 most-downloaded open robotics models on the Hugging Face Hub, including vision-language-action models, refreshed daily, which gives a sense of where open model development is concentrating.

The clearest ROI evidence comes from operators rather than independent studies. Samsara's 380,000+ accidents prevented figure is the most concrete number in the material. Aurora's quoted partners describe the Werner pilot as impressive and emphasize safety and efficiency benefits, with one quote noting autonomous trucks will give drivers better lives by handling lengthier and less desirable routes. Aurora also cites a projection that freight volumes will grow five fold between 2010 and 2050, framing autonomous transport as a necessity rather than an innovation. Waymo's safety hub is described in the sourced points as the most complete public evidence base from an AV operator, with published methodology and crash-rate comparisons.

The regulatory posture is active and, in places, newly codified. The International Maritime Organization adopted the International Code of Safety for Maritime Autonomous Surface Ships (MASS Code) in May 2026, with it coming into effect on 1 July 2026. The IMO notes the Code is voluntary guidance for now, goal-based and technology-neutral, and that at present there are no commercially operating, internationally trading SOLAS cargo ships running autonomously or remotely controlled, though trials have demonstrated feasibility. EASA's Artificial Intelligence Roadmap 2.0 outlines a human-centric approach to AI in aviation, with a living document amended once a year and a path toward conceptual guidance and rulemaking. The American Trucking Associations, representing more than 37,000 members through a federation of 50 state trucking associations, tracks autonomous trucking policy and works to influence government policy on the industry's behalf.

For a reader deciding whether to deploy, the material suggests a split. Telematics, predictive analytics, and AI-assisted safety systems are commercially deployed at scale today, with Samsara's 20,000+ operations as evidence. Autonomous freight and maritime systems remain in pilot, trial, or early regulatory phases, with the IMO's MASS Code only recently in force and EASA's aviation roadmap still evolving toward rulemaking. The Census trend from 7.9% to 13.0% shows adoption broadening, but the regulatory gates for the most ambitious autonomy remain firmly in place.

https://www.samsara.com/.brief: Samsara claims its connected operations platform supports more than 20,000 operations in improving safety, cutting costs, and running smarter. The platform analyzes data to provide AI-driven alerts, predictive analytics, and actionable insights that help spot risks and optimize operations. According to Samsara, its AI-powered dash cams, real-time in-cab alerts, automated coaching, and other safety technologies have prevented over 380,000 accidents. The system includes cameras and video AI, multicam support, driver experience tools, driver coaching, drowsiness detection, safety reporting & insights, and equipment management.

https://www.trucking.org/.brief: ATA, the American Trucking Association, says it is the largest and most comprehensive national trade association for trucking. It reports that Miguel Corral, a UPS driver, was named Bendix Grand Champion at the 2026 National Truck Driving & Step Van Championships. ATA says it has more than 37,000 members, including carriers, suppliers, shippers, and professionals, and that it works to influence government policy, educate stakeholders, and host events that bring together all parts of the industry.

https://www.wartsila.com/.brief: Wärtsilä claims it is a global leader in innovative technologies and lifecycle solutions for the marine and energy markets. The company says it already has most of the technology needed to decarbonise, from engines that can run flexibly on low- and zero-carbon fuels to AI-driven predictive analytics. Wärtsilä is using these tools to help customers take the next step on their decarbonisation journey.

https://www.easa.europa.eu/en/domains/re.brief: The EASA has published an Artificial Intelligence Roadmap 2.0 that outlines the Agency's approach to safety and ethical considerations for AI in aviation. The roadmap provides an action plan for the EASA AI Programme, including conceptual guidance and anticipated rulemaking activities, and serves as a basis for stakeholder discussions. As a living document, it will be updated annually and refined through stakeholder exchanges and the Agency's ongoing practical work on AI development.

https://www.imo.org/en/MediaCentre/HotTo.brief: The IMO introduced a new International Code of Safety for Maritime Autonomous Surface Ships (MASS Code) in May 2026, which became effective on 1 July 2026. A ship is considered a MASS only when autonomous or remote technologies replace or support crew functions and it holds a valid MASS Safety Certificate; enhanced automation alone does not qualify. The Code offers voluntary, technology-neutral guidance that complements existing regulations and defines operating conditions, limits, and responses when those limits are exceeded, creating a “goal-based framework” for safe design, operation, and certification. Trials under interim MSC 110 guidelines in June 2019 have shown that larger remotely controlled and autonomous ships are feasible, and while no SOLAS cargo ships are yet operating autonomously, the IMO anticipates commercial service in the near future with a gradual evolution toward more advanced MASS. An IMO seminar in April 2024 addressed the implications, challenges, and opportunities of MASS for ports and public authorities.

https://theworldofai.org/ai-ecosystem/te.brief: The page presents a catalogue of the 1,000 most-downloaded open robotics models on the Hugging Face Hub, listing each model’s licence, download count, and release date. It states the list is refreshed daily and sorted by all-time downloads using the Hugging Face Hub public API. Each entry links to its corresponding model page on the Hub. The page also notes it was last verified on 2026-09-23.
